Madam / Dear Sir,

Master Direction on Digital Payment System Security Controls and Customer Protection Guidelines

Please refer to Master Direction DPSS.CO.PD.No.1164/02.14.003/2021-22 dated February 18, 2021 on Digital Payment Security Controls. With rapid growth in retail digital payments across Unified Payments Interface (UPI), Immediate Payment Service (IMPS), National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT), and card networks, the Reserve Bank of India has updated the regulatory architecture to reinforce technical resilience, safeguard consumer interests, and enhance multi-layered fraud mitigation controls.

1. SCOPE AND APPLICABILITY:
These directions are issued under Section 10(2) read with Section 18 of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 (Act 51 of 2007). All regulated payment entities, banking companies, and settlement intermediaries operating within India must adhere strictly to the mandates laid down herein.

2. MANDATORY TWO-FACTOR AUTHENTICATION ARCHITECTURE:
All digital transactions initiated through customer-facing payment interfaces must require explicit Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). 
- Factor 1: Knowledge factor (PIN, password, or security passphrase known strictly to the consumer).
- Factor 2: Possession factor (Time-based One-Time Password [OTP], device binding certificate, or hardware cryptographic token).
Regulated entities must ensure that dynamic OTP messages transmitted via SMS, email, or in-app push explicitly state: (a) the exact transaction debit amount, (b) the beneficiary merchant identity, and (c) an unequivocal security warning stating 'Never share this OTP with bank personnel or callers'. Regulated entities must terminate payment sessions upon three consecutive failed authentication attempts.

3. RISK-BASED TRANSACTION MONITORING AND VELOCITY CHECKS:
Regulated entities shall deploy real-time behavioral fraud monitoring solutions capable of evaluating:
- Deviation from customer historical spending patterns;
- Unusual geo-location leaps and simultaneous logins across divergent IP clusters;
- High-velocity peer-to-peer transfers following recent mobile number or password modifications.
Upon detecting anomalous behavioral triggers, entities must enforce stepped-up authentication or temporary cooling-off periods (maximum four hours) prior to processing high-value fund transfers exceeding designated operational limits.

4. REVISED TIMELINES FOR LIMITED CUSTOMER LIABILITY:
Customer liability in unauthorized electronic transactions shall be determined in accordance with the following criteria:
(a) Zero Customer Liability: Customer liability shall be nil when the unauthorized transaction occurs due to contributory fraud, negligence, or deficiency on the part of the bank, or where a third-party breach occurs within the payment system and the customer notifies the bank within three (3) working days of receiving the transaction alert.
(b) Limited Customer Liability: Where the customer notifies the bank within four to seven (4-7) working days, maximum liability shall be capped at INR 10,000 for standard savings bank accounts and INR 25,000 for credit facilities.
(c) Beyond Seven Days: Customer liability shall be governed by the bank's board-approved customer compensation policy.

5. AUDIT TRAIL, RECORD RETENTION, AND GRIEVANCE ESCALATION:
Regulated entities must maintain unalterable, cryptographically signed audit logs of all transaction authorization requests, user session timestamps, IP addresses, and customer communication dispatches for a minimum retention duration of ten (10) years. Customer dispute redressal desks must provide an acknowledgment number within twenty-four hours of dispute lodgment and resolve consumer grievances within thirty (30) calendar days.

6. COMPLIANCE CERTIFICATION AND BOARD OVERSIGHT:
Chief Risk Officers and Chief Information Security Officers (CISO) of all regulated banks shall submit a quarterly compliance certificate confirming adherence to these directives to the Chief General Manager, Department of Payment and Settlement Systems, Reserve Bank of India, Mumbai. Non-compliance shall attract penal actions under Section 26 of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act.

Yours faithfully,
(Dr. Sunita Venkatraman)
